title: PRD validation analysis
description: The prd-validation workflow's contracts. Each lens is one specialist's job and its result is one $defs entry here: requirement-classifier (ClassificationResult), ambiguity-detector (AmbiguityResult), completeness-checker (CompletenessResult), requirements-conflict-detector (ConflictResult), constraint-extractor (ConstraintResult), domain-boundary-validator (BoundaryResult), requirements-clarifier (ClarificationResult) and, when the run names a BRD, brd-traceability-auditor (TraceabilityResult). Each writes its candidate, which jsonartifact.py validates and publishes. The workflow merges the lens results into Analysis (TracedAnalysis when the run names a BRD), published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation.json; it then records each technical rule no document states in the matrix and fails the PRD only on a blocker finding. Every issue, question and detail field stays under 40 words.

Severity.description: `blocker` fails the PRD; `info` is for an absence that may legitimately arrive as its own later PRD.

requirement.description: The requirement's id as the PRD writes it (R1, R2, … in document order where it gives none).

RequirementClass.description: One requirement the PRD states, classified. A requirement that states both a business outcome and a technical rule is two entries with the same `id`.

id.description: The requirement's id as the PRD writes it; R1, R2, … in document order where it gives none.

class.description: `business`: what a user, the business or a regulation needs, stated as an outcome that holds however the system is built. `technical`: a rule about HOW the system is built (a named technology, resource, configuration, construct, network path or engineering standard), which belongs in the architecture, not in a PRD.

reason.description: One line on the classification; for `archCoverage: unchecked`, what the matrix command printed.

governs.description: Technical: the kind of thing the rule governs (for example "S3 bucket"). Business: "".

rule.description: Technical: the rule as a condition on that thing ("where the design has an S3 bucket, the bucket is versioned"). The workflow records it in the matrix as a constraint when `archCoverage` is `absent`. Business: "".

archCoverage.description: Technical: `covered` when a constraint stated in an `effective` document, or a heading of an `effective` document, states the rule (as `atw-matrix find --kinds constraint,document` and `atw-matrix node` return it); `absent` when the lookups return no entry that states it; `unchecked` only when the matrix command fails. Business: `n/a`.

archRefs.description: Technical and covered: the id of each entry that states the rule, a document as `<id>#<heading>`. Otherwise [].

source.description: Where the PRD states or implies it.

Traceability.description: Informational only, never a judgment of the PRD: the mapping of each PRD requirement to the BRD objective(s) it serves. A requirement that traces to no objective is never a defect.

traceable.description: Whether a mapping could be built at all; not a verdict on the PRD.

orphanRequirements.description: Requirements that map to no objective.

unimplementedObjectives.description: Objectives no requirement serves, only where this single PRD could plausibly have served them.

ClassificationResult.description: What the requirement-classifier writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-requirement-class.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/requirement-class.json.

AmbiguityResult.description: What the ambiguity-detector writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-ambiguity.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/ambiguity.json.

CompletenessResult.description: What the completeness-checker writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-completeness.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/completeness.json.

ConflictResult.description: What the requirements-conflict-detector writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-conflict.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/conflict.json.

ConstraintResult.description: What the constraint-extractor writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-constraints.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/constraints.json.

BoundaryResult.description: What the domain-boundary-validator writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-boundary.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/boundary.json.

ClarificationResult.description: What the requirements-clarifier writes: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-clarification.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/clarification.json.

TraceabilityResult.description: What the brd-traceability-auditor writes when the run names a BRD: the candidate <artifacts.dir>/candidates/prd-validation-traceability.json, published as <artifacts.dir>/prd-validation/traceability.json.

Analysis.description: The merged analysis the workflow writes from the lens results (<artifacts.dir>/prd-validation.json).

requirementClasses.description: Every requirement the PRD states, once each, classified by the requirement-classifier.

ambiguities.description: Requirements whose user-observable behavior is genuinely unclear, contradictory or open to two incompatible readings, each with a concrete clarification, found by the ambiguity-detector.

completenessGaps.description: Requirements missing an actor, a trigger or action, an observable user outcome or a behavioral acceptance criterion, found by the completeness-checker.

conflicts.description: Sets of requirements whose WHAT cannot all hold, found by the requirements-conflict-detector.

constraints.description: The explicit and implied constraints the PRD imposes: regulatory, business, platform, policy, extracted by the constraint-extractor.

boundaryFindings.description: Requirements that make this feature own behavior another feature or service owns, or that sit in more than one bounded context, found by the domain-boundary-validator.

clarifications.description: Open BUSINESS questions the author must answer before the PRD can be specified, unresolved, raised by the requirements-clarifier. A technical gap is never one.

summary.description: A plain-language readout, under 120 words, of the PRD's readiness for downstream specification: the counts of classified requirements and of findings by severity, which the workflow composes from the lens results.

TracedAnalysis.description: The analysis of a run that names a BRD: `traceability` is required.
